chunks: O believers, expend of what We have given you before the day arrives on which there will be no barter, and no friendship or intercession, and those who are disbelievers will be the sinners.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of spending before the Day of Judgment according to Surah Al-Baqarah?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse (Ayat al-Zakat) is often cited to establish the obligation of voluntary charity (Sadaqat) alongside obligatory alms (Zakat), emphasizing that wealth is a divine trust requiring timely distribution. The mention of 'no intercession' (Shafa'ah) is particularly significant in Shia theology, where it is understood that intercession on the Day of Judgment is contingent upon God's permission and the merit of the intercessor, rather than being an automatic right. This underscores the urgency of accumulating spiritual capital through charity before the final reckoning, where material wealth becomes useless.
